description: Rust crate eindir-core, with Python, C and C++ bindings, of primitives for bounded optimisation and sampling on R^D: objectives over box bounds, Halton point sets, gradients, a generalized Langevin equation (GLE) thermostat and Chebyshev surrogates. The anneal optimiser is built on it.
rules: From Python use eindir._core.Bounds and eindir._core.PyObjective. eindir does not export Bounds, Objective, GleThermostat or AdditiveSurrogate, though Python examples on five pages of the manual import them from it.
Only the Rust crate has the GLE thermostat, the surrogates, the gradient adapters and the builtin test-function types. Write Rust against eindir-core for them.
eindir._core takes contiguous float64 NumPy arrays only. Lists, integer arrays and strided views raise TypeError.

Rust panics reach Python as pyo3_runtime.PanicException, a BaseException that except Exception misses. Three calls panic: Bounds with low > high and Bounds.clip of a wrong-length point, both since 0.6.0, and a PyObjective called from another thread.

Read the version from eindir._core.__version__, since eindir.__version__ does not exist. Releases lag main, so check cargo info eindir-core and pip index versions eindir before relying on a new feature.
In Rust, DifferentiableObjective has no blanket impl, so add an empty impl DifferentiableObjective<f64> for T {}. On a type with Objective and Gradient, call Objective::dim(&x).
The C ABI needs DLPack 1.0 headers and the capi feature. Install with cargo cinstall and link against that prefix. A program linked against the cargo cbuild tree cannot load libeindir_core.so.0.7.
eindir_last_error() is per thread and only eindir sets it: a failing callback leaves the previous message and a success does not clear it. Go by the returned status.

Edit the manual in docs/orgmode/*.org. The command pixi run -e docs orgbld writes docs/source/*.rst from it, and git ignores those files. Change the version only in Cargo.toml, then run tools/sync-version.sh.
